title: feat(app-shell): Studio retires the two delegated-admin switches the spec retired (objectui#12406)
body:
Fixes #12406
Clause-②: no

- [x] Adds no product-specific widget, dialog, hook or string (see AGENTS.md › Product-neutral renderer)

## What changes

Studio's permission-set editor stops offering the two delegated-admin switches that `@objectstack/spec` 18 retired. This is item 4 of the maintainer's letter A on objectstack-ai/objectstack#23488 (comment 6181988435): "objectui: Studio's two switches, the help strings, the i18n keys and the pin test retire".

- **`PermissionAdvancedFacets.tsx`.** The "Manage bindings" and "Author env sets" switch rows are gone. "Manage assignments" stays as the control and now writes its key by name, `setScopeDetail({ manageAssignments: !!v })`, instead of through the tuple list's cast to the partial `AdminScope` type. The header docblock names the four live keys. The `AdminScope` docblock now says why the editor strips neither retired key from a loaded scope (the H3 decision below). Two docblock counts ("the six keys", "the other five carry defaults") are corrected, because two of those keys are now tombstones.
- **`i18n.ts`.** The four strings go: `perm.admin.manageBindings` and `perm.admin.authorEnvironmentSets`, in English and Chinese. `perm.admin.help` no longer offers to "manage bindings", in either language. I read the ruling's "help strings" as this text, the only Studio help string that names a retired right.
- **`PermissionAdvancedFacets.adminScopeAnchor.test.tsx`.** The inert-switch case now covers the one remaining manage switch. A new describe block pins the retirement (see Tests).
- **`.changeset/12406-retire-admin-switches.md`.** `@object-ui/app-shell` patch, with the Clause-② reading in words.

**Clause-②: no.** `PermissionAdvancedFacets` and the metadata-admin dictionary are not on `@object-ui/app-shell`'s published entry (`exports` has `.` and `./styles.css`; `src/index.ts` exports neither). The change removes two controls that wrote keys the spec already refuses. No published type, prop or export changes.

## Measurements

- **Installable surface**, measured with the spec installed here (`18.0.0-next.2`). `AdminScopeSchema` refuses each retired key with `invalid_type` at its own path, for both `true` and `false`. CONTROL: a scope with the four live keys parses.
- **H1 holds.** The three switches were drawn from a tuple list. The two retired rows are gone, and `manageAssignments` stays.
- **H2 holds.** Outside `CHANGELOG.md`, the workspace has these four strings only in `i18n.ts` and the anchor pin's caption list. The control `manageAssignments` is found in the same files. No other locale pack or reader exists.
- **H4: next.2 tombstones the keys and keeps them.** Both keys stay on the `AdminScope` type, typed as the retired mark: an object whose one key is `'[REMOVED] Key retired: run os validate for its migration.'` with type `never`. The old tuple-list write compiled only because of its cast. The new by-name write lets that type do the refusing. Reverse check: `setScopeDetail({ manageBindings: !!v })` was written at the switch, and `tsc --noEmit` turned red with `TS2322: Type 'boolean' is not assignable to type` that retired mark. The file was then restored by `ablation-replace.mjs`, and its blob equals HEAD.
- **H3: the facet round-trips the stored scope verbatim.** Measured with a throwaway mount of the facet (not committed). The draft was `{"businessUnit":"east","manageAssignments":true,"manageBindings":true,"authorEnvironmentSets":false}`. After one "Include subtree" flip it reads `{…, "manageBindings":true, "authorEnvironmentSets":false, "includeSubtree":true}`. `setScope` spreads the stored object, and the host's whole-record Save sends `draft.adminScope` whether or not the facet was touched.
- **H3, the server side.** Read on objectstack `0af559e`: the metadata protocol's layered read (the overlay row) and its draft read both pass the stored row through `convertStoredItem`, then `applyConversionsToStoredItem` (retired entries included), whose conversion `permission-admin-scope-binding-authoring-removed` drops both keys. The spec half was measured here with the installed spec: `applyConversionsToStoredItem('permission', …)` turns that same stored scope into `{"businessUnit":"east","manageAssignments":true}` and emits two notices from that conversion. The raw stored set fails `PermissionSetSchema`; the rehydrated one passes. The save door validates strictly and replays no conversion, so a body that still carried either key would be answered `422 INVALID_METADATA` at the key.

## H3 decision: Studio does not strip the two keys

Two options. **A**: mirror this file's RLS `priority` precedent and strip both keys in the facet's write path. **B**: strip nothing, and leave the server's stored-row conversion as the one place they are dropped. **Chosen: B.** Reasons, axis by axis:

- **Real business need (measured).** After this PR nothing in Studio authors either key. The only way one could reach Save is a loaded draft that carries it. The server's overlay and draft reads already drop both keys before the body reaches Studio, and a built artifact is either converted forward at the artifact door or refused at boot. On an 18 server, a strip in the facet has no input to act on.
- **Long-term soundness.** A would be a second, client-side copy of the spec's retirement list, which every future retirement would also have to edit by hand. B keeps the one seam the spec registered (ADR-0087 D2, `registered`). A strip in the facet would also only cover facet edits: the host's whole-record Save sends the scope untouched, so A could not deliver "saves without them" from inside this file.
- **Preventing AI errors.** B keeps the refusal loud. Any body that still carries either key, from any producer, is answered with a 422 that names the key and points at `os validate`. A would silently drop it on the client, which is the consumer-side tolerance the frame ranks below a strict contract.
- **No scope spread at the startup stage.** B adds no code and no gate, and the retirement is immediate. A adds a strip and a pin for a path with no pull.

A's case rests on this file's RLS `priority` strip. That strip was written when Studio's own Add button seeded the retired key into new policies, so this editor was the producer. Here the producer was the switches, and they are gone.

## Tests

The new describe is `PermissionAdvancedFacets · the retired delegated-admin keys (objectui#12406)`, mounted as the Access pillar mounts the facet (`only="admin"`). Switches are found by role, not by caption:
- **CONTROL.** The installed spec refuses each retired key at its own path, `false` included.
- **Draws the manage-assignments switch and neither retired switch.** The captions of the switches in the section are exactly Include subtree and Manage assignments.
- **Flipping every switch it draws writes a scope the spec accepts, carrying neither retired key.** It checks the key set, a `safeParse` success, and the exact written object.

**Ablation** (wrap mode, `ablation-replace.mjs` from objectstack). The two retired rows were put back exactly as they were on `main` (tuple list, cast included). The run read `Tests 2 failed | 10 passed (12)`: the two new pins went red (`expected [ 'perm.admin.includeSubtree', …(3) ]` and `expected [ 'manageBindings', …(1) ] to deeply equal []`). Restore was proven: blob after restore equals blob at HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty. The test imports the component from source, so no build sits between the mutation and the run.

All of the following ran on head `165e820`, the final commit. Every exit code was captured before any pipe.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/`: exit 0, `Test Files 509 passed (509)`, `Tests 5742 passed | 1 skipped (5743)`. It held the shared verify lock for 940s on a shared 4-core box.
- `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2`: exit 0, `Tasks: 28 successful, 28 total`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`: exit 0. The output echoes `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`. The test project includes `src/**/*.test.tsx`, so the new cases are type-checked.
- `pnpm check:changeset-claims` 0 · `pnpm changeset:check` 0 · `pnpm check:test-path-roots` 0 · `pnpm check:spec-symbols` 0 · `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` 0 · `pnpm check:new-line-citations` 0 · `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the 4 paths: 0, `NOT GOVERNED`.
- eslint on the three changed source files: exit 0, with 0 errors and 3 warnings. All 3 warnings are on lines this diff does not touch (the `setDraft` prop's `any`, and a `setErrorMap` call inside an effect).
- Not run locally: the whole `packages/app-shell/` suite and the repo-wide lint. Both are left to CI, as the dispatch said.

## Acceptance notes

- `docs/adr/0056-permission-editing-studio.md` still names `manageBindings` and `authorEnvironmentSets` in the `AdminScopeSchema` bullet ("the exact target shape for the admin_scope editor"). It is governed text, so it is not edited here (Tier S/H). Carrier: none in objectui. The ruling's item 5 Tier H docs PR covers ADR-0090 and ADR-0086 in objectstack, not this ADR.
- `packages/app-shell/src/__tests__/spec-symbol-parity.test.ts` has a comment, "…and the other five are defaulted". Two of those five are now tombstones. It is a comment, not an assertion, and the assertions still hold. It is outside this card's file surface and is noted only.
- The host's whole-record Save (`PermissionMatrixEditor`) sends `draft.adminScope` as loaded. That is safe only because the server's reads drop the two keys (H3). It is recorded here as the boundary of the H3 decision, not as a defect.

The session is `https://claude.ai/code/session_011K9g23W67dy2zwnyzaoB6o`.
